narr: An upper level disturbance crossed through West Virginia from the west on August 19th, leading to showers with moderate to heavy rainfall expanding in coverage across the area throughout the day. Due to the rainfall received with the remnants of Tropical Storm Fred the previous day, soil across the area was already saturated in many locations. This caused several locations to be more susceptible to flooding issues. High water was observed over roads in multiple locations throughout West Virginia, with some of these roads becoming impassable for a time.
ev: Panther Lane was under water southwest of the town of Sandyville.
High water was observed over Sand Fork Road near the town of Gallipolis Ferry.
High water flowed over Jericho Road near the city of Point Pleasant.
Route 4 and Cutlip Fork Road in the town of Gassaway were both impassable due to high water.
Multiple locations along Exchange Road near the town of Exchange had high water over the road. A few of these locations were impassable for a brief time.
High water flowed over both lanes of Lick Creek Road in the town of Danville.
High water flowed over Frontage Road near the Danville Animal Clinic.
Flooding was observed near the community of East Lynn.
Flooding was observed along Mill Creek northwest of the community of Radnor.

County Route 16 near the intersection with Jericho Road and County Route 16 near the town of Gallipolis Ferry were both closed due to high water over the roads. One lane of WV Route 2 was also blocked by high water near Gallipolis Ferry.
Flatwoods Road was impassable due to flash flooding north of the town of Flatwoods.
High water flowed across Route 21 to the north of the city of Ripley.
Flatwoods Road was under water in the town of Flatwoods.
